answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network anchors identity to cryptographic stake burning using a superlinear cost curve C(n) = k * n^2 for n active identities. Like immovable basalt resisting a rising tide of malicious nodes, this quadratic burn imposes extreme economic friction. An attacker attempting to flood consensus finds their capital drained exponentially faster than shifting a desert dune, rendering mass node replication unprofitable.
